decisions.quote:
When comparing regression analyses, three areas of difference were noted between our study and Luo et
al.’s (2022) results. The first area of difference is seen in applicant rank. Luo et al. found that student
applicants were more efficient than early, middle, or late career applicants, while our research found that
faculty applicants may have experienced fewer days between approval and expenditure than graduate
students, staff, or postdoctoral applicants, but that the overall category does not appear statistically
significant. Next, data from our study appear to indicate that returning applicants experienced more days
between approval and expenditure than new applicants, e.g. those who had not sought funding before,
while Luo et al. found that return applicant status was not significant.
decisions.reason: Although the conclusion affirms Luo et al.’s (2022) hypothesis that limiting funding consideration to accepted and published articles improves fund efficiency, this is only one comparison rather than an overall replication verdict, and the regression replication explicitly reports key differences from Luo et al.’s findings regarding applicant rank, return applicant status, and co-authorship.
